feature: One Zoom lane per track on a long edit
summary: A track's zooms now share one Zoom row under it, bars side by side, so the hour-long edit shows one Zoom row under V1 instead of 126 and the Background and Music tracks stay in sight.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. The button on step 1 opens your own copy of the 60 minute reference edit in Photonz Dev; once made, File > Open reaches it too (Cmd-Shift-G, ~/Library/Caches/Photonz Reference Edit/Photonz Dev).

try.do: Open the 60 minute reference edit in Photonz Dev with the button below and look under V1: one Zoom row, then Background and Music.
Zoom the timeline in on the first minute (= a few times).
Click the 150% bar on the Zoom row: it picks that zoom and puts its box on the picture.
Shift click the 190% bar, which sits on another clip: both are picked.
Click the word Zoom at the left of the row: every zoom on the track is picked and the panel reads them together.
Draw a box across the Zoom row and a clip: the zooms it touches are picked with the clip.

evaluate: Does one Zoom row under the track read clearly as the zooms of all its clips?
Is Shift click on a bar of another clip adding to the pick what you expect?
Should the label pick every zoom on the track, or only the ones on the clip under the playhead?
At the whole hour the bars are 3 point slivers. Is that enough to see where the zooms are?
rough: The mock (video-zoom-wt.html) draws a punch-in as Scale and Centre key lanes, two rows under V1; the app's zoom bars on a Zoom row come from a-zoom-region-that-frames-a-spot-and-can-follow, and this task keeps them to one row, within the mock's two.

On the hour-long edit the panel takes about a second to show the picked zoom's rows after a click; at half a second the walk's picture still showed an empty panel. Left in the task log rather than filed: the open task the-timeline-of-an-hour-long-edit-scrolls-zooms owns the long edit's speed.
At the whole-hour view each bar is a faint 3 point sliver on the dark lane; they read as ticks, not bars, until the timeline is zoomed in.
